deepdive.sec: Enterprise SaaS / Loyalty & Customer Engagement Infrastructure

bull_bear.body: Active M&A roll-up strategy (SessionM deal at ~0.5x revenue); Cash generation strong (200% FCF to PAT ratio); Capital used for platform upgrades and indemnity collections rather than dividends/buybacks currently.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Integration execution risk on SessionM (margin accretion delayed if migration slows); Concentration risk in large enterprise clients; Competition from mega-vendors/agencies; Currency fluctuations (significant US exposure); Dependency on successful AI monetization (aiRA).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and aggressive on M&A; Transparent about one-offs (indemnity income); Emphasizes 'system of record' stickiness; Bullish on AI multiplying platform value rather than replacing it; Pragmatic on near-term margin mix due to acquisitions.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The INR 25 Cr one-time income masks underlying PAT growth trajectory (normalized PAT grew 51% in Q4); AI stack (aiRA) is shifting pricing model from subscription to outcome-based (per question/analysis), potentially unlocking higher NRR; Migration of acquired customers is now AI-accelerated, reducing the typical 2-year synergy timeline.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- M&A is the primary capital-deployment engine and is judged on cash payback — a stated "4-5 year cash pay back engine", with SessionM called "an efficient acquisition with a strong likelihood of delivering payback in the near term".
- Return metrics improving off a low base: ROCE 2.8% (FY25), 3.0% (FY26), 5.2% (Q1 TTM FY27); ROIC 3.2%, 4.8%, 7.3%; CROIC 17.4%, 21.8%, 23.2%; RONW 3.0%, 7.4%, 5.9%.
- Capital Employed remained broadly stable at ₹10,676.2 Mn (Q1 TTM FY27) versus ₹10,682.2 Mn (FY26), with Invested Capital rising to ₹5,986.2 Mn from ₹5,494.0 Mn.
- High depreciation and amortisation "reflects recent acquisitions (Rewards, Brierley, Kognitiv, SessionM)" — an acquisition-driven, non-cash drag on reported PAT.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Loyalty Stack: ~90% of revenue, system-of-record, per-member/transaction pricing; Engage (Marketing Automation): 5-7% of revenue; Rewards: 5-7% of revenue; aiRA (AI Analytics/Action): Few million USD, fastest growing, replacing Insights, pricing on action/outcome basis.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Named a Leader in The Forrester Wave: Loyalty Platforms, Q4 2025, with the deck claiming "Highest among all vendors in both Current Offering and Strategy" and a "5/5 Score in 22 out of 27 Criteria".
- Scale as of June 30, 2026: 465+ brands, 2.7 billion+ consumers on the platform, 19 global offices, 53 countries, 25 Fortune 500 customers and 99.997% product uptime.
- Forrester is quoted saying the platform "supports complex programs, including coalition, subscription, and gamified formats" and that customers praise "usability, AI enablement, and promotion flexibility".
- Retention is the headline moat metric: for the trailing twelve months ending June 30, 2026, Total (blended) NRR is 113%, Organic NRR 111% and Inorganic NRR 120%; the deck argues Organic NRR is "the clearest retention metric" since acquired cohorts only normalise after platform migration.
- Business model framed as subscription-led — subscription revenue was 94.5% of Q1 FY27 revenue, up from 89.4% in Q4 FY26, led by the higher subscription mix in the acquired SessionM business.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Cyber fraud] Between June 24 and July 2, 2026 SessionM Czech Republic s.r.o., a step-down subsidiary, was subjected to a sophisticated social engineering fraud in which perpetrators impersonated the Group CEO and a purported M&A counsel, inducing a senior executive to effect unauthorised remittances of ₹333.9 Mn (EUR 3.05 Mn) to third-party bank accounts in Hong Kong and Singapore; the full amount is provided for as an exceptional expense pending potential insurance settlement.
- [Fraud recovery] Criminal complaints were filed in Czechia on July 3, 2026 and in Singapore and Hong Kong on July 4, 2026; approximately ₹47.0 Mn (EUR 428K) has been frozen in Singapore; Hong Kong exposure of EUR 2.07 Mn is subject to court proceedings that counsel estimates may take approximately 6-8 months.
- [Forensic and insurance] KPMG (Forensic Services), Prague team, is conducting an independent investigation with no evidence of malware or device compromise so far and a final report expected later in August; the insurance claim is notified under the Crime Insurance Policy with coverage indicated under Social Engineering (CEO Fraud) provisions, expected to conclude in approximately 5-6 months.
- [Guidance] "The business is on track to deliver our earlier FY27 guidance: ₹10,650 Mn. revenue and ₹1,720 Mn. Adjusted EBITDA."
- [Non-GAAP] The deck flags that Adjusted EBITDA, ARR and NRR are non-GAAP measures not defined under Ind AS, IFRS or U.S. GAAP, and that market-size and competitive-position data is sourced from third parties (Zinnov, Forrester) and has not been independently verified.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross margins improved ~100 bps YoY to ~65-70% range on core platform; Acquired stacks start at ~30% GM, migrate to ~65% GM; Non-COGS costs grew 14% vs 23% revenue growth showing operating leverage; US sales team ramp increased per-employee cost despite flat headcount (+1% YoY).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: FY27 revenue expected to cross INR 1,000-1,050 Cr (driven by SessionM consolidation + organic); Margin: Core organic business targeting 25-30% steady-state EBITDA, but consolidated margins may dip slightly in FY27 due to SessionM integration before expanding; Order Inflow: Targeting INR 70-80 Cr annual new organic ACV plus large enterprise wins; Capex/Commissioning: AI-led migration tools expected to accelerate customer upgrades from acquired stacks to Capillary platform within 12-18 months.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Run-rate revenue of INR 765 Cr as of March 31, 2026 (excludes SessionM); FY26 New ACV wins of INR 121 Cr; Significant pipeline from SessionM's 40+ logos (5 Fortune 500) pending migration.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion of TAM beyond system-of-record into intelligence and action spaces via aiRA; Cross-selling AI stack to 25% of existing base; Geographic expansion (US momentum); Vertical-specific deepening (Retail, Travel, Healthcare, BFSI).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Capillary delivered strong Q4FY26 organic growth (26% YoY) and margin expansion (19% adj. EBITDA) driven by 114% organic NRR and AI stack uptake, while the May 1 closure of the $35M SessionM acquisition sets up a FY27 revenue beat (>INR 1,000 Cr) albeit with near-term margin dilution as migration synergies realize over 12-18 months.

risks.note: Company operates in a hybrid work environment amid an evolving cybersecurity threat landscape. It holds ISO 27001:2022 and PCI DSS 4.0.1 certifications and completes annual SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 1 Type 2 attestations, but is still working toward HITRUST certification, indicating this remains an active, unresolved risk area for a SaaS platform business handling customer and consumer data.

The Company's revenue and operations are heavily linked to foreign currencies through its numerous overseas step-down subsidiaries and export-oriented service delivery, with foreign exchange inflows substantially exceeding outflows disclosed for FY26, exposing it to currency translation and transaction risk.

The Risk Management Committee's framework explicitly identifies financial, operational, sectoral, sustainability (environmental, social and governance), information and cybersecurity risks as the principal categories facing the Company, without further company-specific elaboration provided in this section of the report.
